newsitem.title: USA: Valspar sees $2.93 a share for 1997 net.
newsitem.headline: Valspar sees $2.93 a share for 1997 net.

text.p: Valspar Corp said Wednesday that chances of hitting $2.93 a share in fiscal 1997 earnings are "pretty good." In fiscal 1996, Valspar earned $2.52.

"Our long-range target is a 15 percent (annual increase in earnings per share) and the 16 percent increase (to $2.93) is pretty close to that," said Richard Rompala, chief execiutive officer. "As of today, things look pretty good," he said after the company's annual shareholders meeting here.
Rompala also said he expects Valspar's fiscal 1997 sales to exceed $1 billion.

"Over the long term, we've been targeting eight to ten percent per year internal growth in sales and seven to 10 percent in growth from acquisitions," he said. "It's an aggressive target but we intend to hit sales in excess of $1 billion this year."
Valspar sales last year totaled $859.8 million.
Rompala noted that sales generated by the company's packaging group will account for about one third of its business this year, with the addition of Coates Brothers on a full year basis.
Last year the packaging group accounted for 27 percent of total sales. Valspar is in the process of acquiring Coates Brothers, a can coatings and metal decorating inks business.
He also said international sales as percent of total sales are expected to double in fiscal 1997 to about 10 percent.
